newsitem.title: USA: Ford July U.S. light vehicle sales rise 5.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Ford July U.S. light vehicle sales rise 5.1 percent.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. reported a 5.1 percent increase in July U.S. car and light truck sales on Tuesday, helping to fuel a mid-summer rebound for the U.S. auto industry.
Big sport utility vehicles pulled Ford's truck sales for the month up 14.9 percent from a year ago to 200,342 units, marking the 11th consecutive monthly increase.
Ford's car sales fell 5.4 percent to 153,407 units, but executives at the No. 2 automaker said they saw some encouraging signs, including an improvement in car sales to consumers.
Sales to fleet customers, including daily rental fleets, were down 13 percent for the month, accounting for the entire car sales decline, the company said.

"Obviously, we're delighted by our continuing success in trucks," said Robert Rewey, Ford's group vice president of sales, service and marketing. "Not so obvious is that our car sales are picking up -- more than we expected. For the first time in a long time, dealers are telling us they should have ordered more cars."

Sales of Ford's best-selling Taurus declined 11.6 percent, putting the car further behind the Toyota Camry in the race for America's best-selling car. Year-to-date sales of the Taurus were down 7.1 percent to 206,426 units, compared with 239,041 for the Camry and 194,910 for the third-place Honda Accord.

Although final industry sales results were not yet available, the Ford results were expected to give the industry an overall July sales gain of 5 percent over a year ago and a seasonally adjusted annual sales rate in the range of 15.5 million units, following three consecutive months below 15 million units.
The sales rate in July 1996 was 14.7 million units.

On Friday, Chrysler Corp. reported a 9.3 percent drop in vehicle sales, with domestic car sales down 12.3 percent and domestic light truck sales off 7.6 percent. General Motors Corp., meanwhile, said July sales rose by a surprisingly strong 6.7 percent, with domestic car sales up 2.4 percent and domestic light truck sales up 11.5 percent.

Honda Motor Co Ltd.'s U.S. sales during July rose an impressive 31.8 percent, while Toyota Motor Corp.'s rose 14.6 percent. Nissan Motor Co. Ltd., however, said its sales fell 6.9 percent and Mazda Motor Corp. reported flat sales for the month.
Ford's Rewey said he is encouraged by the U.S. economy's performance.

"The Conference Board's July survey showed that consumer confidence remains high and that consumers plan to purchase more big-ticket items like autos and appliances," he said. "This suggests that 1997's industry sales will be in the mid-15 million range for the fourth consecutive year."
Ford shares were up 18.75 cents to $41.4375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading. GM stock was up
$1.125 to $63.8125, while Chrysler shares were up 37.5 cents to $36.9375.
